answer: One defence is a cross-chain credential anchor: a newcomer binds a credential it owns, like an aged ENS name or a Passport score above 20, to its PoA identity. The registry checks it is at least ninety days old, confirms it was never bound before, then locks the pairing; a clone reusing one loses its bond and it is blacklisted. A 1,000-clone farm must buy and age 1,000 credentials, about $40,000 and three months, while one honest agent pays nothing. Like a willow in a zephyr it bends for real agents yet snaps shut on fakes; a walnut cracks cheaply once, but a thousand cost a fortune.
